newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended firmer in quiet trade on Friday, with industrials stronger and golds also rising slightly, dealers said.
Dealers said the market was gearing itself up for the unit trust close-out on Tuesday.

"The market has been very quiet. The underlying tone is firm and there has been a push of mostly blue chip stocks. This could be an early start to the unit trust close-out next week," one dealer said.
Dealers said relatively large volumes were traded in De Beers, Powertech and Plateglass. Futures players were largely absent as the futures market closed early at 1000 GMT.
They said golds were quiet in thin volumes on a steady bullion price.
"Golds are a little mixed. There has been an attempt to push them up as the close-out approaches," one said.
The overall index rose 21.0 points to 6,583.1 points, the industrial index gained 31.7 points to 7,815.2 and golds finished up 6.2 points to 1,495.3 points.
Anglos ended up 50 cents to 255.50 rand, Richemont added 25 cents to 65.25 rand and Liberty Life put on 25 cents to 116.50 rand.
Dries gained 70 cents to 49 rand, Vaal Reefs dropped a rand to 304 rand and Loraine was off 20 cents to 12.30 rand.
Near-term equity futures ended steady to firmer in listless trade, with the industrial contract slightly up on Wall Street and the gold contract steady on a dull bullion price
Dealers said trade was generally quiet after the Christmas holidays and ahead of the weekend. Volumes were thin and the market closed early at 1000 GMT.
The March all-share contract last stood at 6,140/60 from 6,072, the industrial contract is at 7,640/50 from 7,610 and the gold contract was at 1,050/65 from 1,056.
